professor.name: Dr. Gupta
professor.text: Many universities now offer courses completely online. Some people think online courses are just as good as courses in a classroom. Others think students learn more when they are physically present. Which kind of course do you think is better for students, and why?

students.name: Andrew
students.text: I prefer online courses because I can watch the lectures when I want. I work part-time, so this flexibility is very important for me.

students.name: Claire
students.text: I learn better in a classroom. When I can ask the teacher a question immediately and talk with classmates, I understand the topic faster.

professor.name: Professor Adams
professor.text: Some schools require students to wear uniforms, while others let students choose their own clothes. Do you think school uniforms are a good idea? Why or why not?

students.name: Maria
students.text: Uniforms are a good idea because students don't feel pressure to wear expensive clothes. Everyone looks the same, so there is less competition.

students.name: Kevin
students.text: I disagree. Clothes are a way to express who you are. Uniforms take away students' freedom to show their personality.

professor.name: Dr. Watson
professor.text: Cities are looking for ways to reduce traffic. One idea is to make public transportation free for everyone. Do you think free public transportation is a good idea? Explain your opinion.

students.name: Julia
students.text: Yes, free buses would encourage people to leave their cars at home. This would reduce traffic and pollution at the same time.

students.name: Marcus
students.text: It sounds nice, but somebody has to pay for it. Taxes would go up, and the service might become worse because there is less money.

professor.name: Professor Lin
professor.text: Some people believe that students should have a part-time job while they are at university. Others think students should focus only on their studies. What is your view?

students.name: Ryan
students.text: A part-time job teaches responsibility and time management. These skills are useful after graduation.

students.name: Aisha
students.text: University is already stressful. If students work too much, their grades will suffer. I think they should focus on studying.

professor.name: Dr. Hassan
professor.text: Social media is now a main source of news for many young people. Do you think getting news from social media is a positive or a negative development? Why?

students.name: Emma
students.text: It is positive because news spreads very quickly, and people can hear different voices, not just big newspapers.

students.name: Victor
students.text: I think it is negative. There is a lot of false information on social media, and many people don't check if a story is true.

professor.name: Professor Rossi
professor.text: Some teachers give homework every day, while others give very little homework. Do you think daily homework helps students learn? Explain your view.

students.name: Hannah
students.text: Daily homework helps us practice what we learned in class. Without it, I would forget things quickly.

students.name: Leo
students.text: Too much homework makes students tired and stressed. Students also need time for sports, family and rest.

professor.name: Dr. Kim
professor.text: Many people now work from home at least part of the week. Do you think working from home is better or worse for employees? Why?

students.name: Sofia
students.text: Working from home saves time because you don't have to travel. People can use that time to rest or be with their families.

students.name: David
students.text: I think it can be lonely. At the office you can talk to colleagues and solve problems together more easily.

professor.name: Professor Mensah
professor.text: Some people say that it is important to learn about history in school. Others think students should spend more time on practical subjects like technology or finance. Which do you think is more important?

students.name: Olivia
students.text: History helps us understand why the world is the way it is today. We can learn from past mistakes.

students.name: Ben
students.text: Practical subjects prepare us for real life. Knowing how to manage money is more useful than remembering dates.

professor.name: Dr. Fischer
professor.text: Some cities have banned cars from their city centers. Do you think this is a good idea? Why or why not?

students.name: Lucia
students.text: It is a great idea. City centers become quieter, cleaner and safer for people who walk or ride bikes.

students.name: Tom
students.text: It could hurt small businesses. If customers can't drive into the center, they might go to shopping malls instead.

professor.name: Professor Tanaka
professor.text: Many students use their phones during class. Some teachers think phones should be completely banned in classrooms. What do you think? Should phones be allowed in class?

students.name: Grace
students.text: Phones should be banned because they distract students. Many people check social media instead of listening.

students.name: Samuel
students.text: Phones can be useful for learning. We can look up words or information quickly. Teachers should teach us to use them responsibly.

professor.name: Dr. Novak
professor.text: Some people think that children should learn a second language from a very young age. Others think it is better to start when they are older. When do you think children should start learning a foreign language?

students.name: Nadia
students.text: Children should start very early because young children learn languages naturally, almost like a game.

students.name: Paul
students.text: I think children should first master their own language. They can start a second language at around ten years old.

professor.name: Professor Walker
professor.text: Some people believe that zoos are important for protecting animals. Others think animals should not be kept in zoos at all. What is your opinion about zoos?

students.name: Chloe
students.text: Good zoos protect endangered animals and teach children to care about nature.

students.name: Ethan
students.text: Even the best zoo is not a natural home. Animals should live in the wild, and we should protect their habitats instead.

professor.name: Dr. Costa
professor.text: Many universities require first-year students to live on campus. Do you think living on campus is important for new students? Why or why not?

students.name: Isabel
students.text: Living on campus helps new students make friends quickly and feel part of the university.

students.name: Noah
students.text: It is often expensive. Students who live near the university should be able to stay at home and save money.

professor.name: Professor Bauer
professor.text: Some people prefer to travel alone, while others prefer to travel with friends or family. Which way of traveling do you think is better, and why?

students.name: Mei
students.text: Traveling alone is better because you can do what you want and you meet more local people.

students.name: Carlos
students.text: I prefer traveling with friends. Sharing experiences makes them more fun, and it is also safer.

professor.name: Dr. Ibrahim
professor.text: Governments spend a lot of money on space exploration. Some people think this money should be used to solve problems on Earth instead. What do you think?

students.name: Alice
students.text: Space research has given us many useful technologies, like satellites for weather forecasts. It is worth the money.

students.name: James
students.text: We have many problems here, like poverty and disease. Solving them should be more important than going to other planets.

professor.name: Professor O'Brien
professor.text: Some students like to study in groups, while others prefer to study alone. Which method do you think is more effective? Explain why.

students.name: Lily
students.text: Group study is effective because classmates can explain things that you don't understand.

students.name: Jack
students.text: I study better alone. In groups, people often start talking about other things and waste time.

professor.name: Dr. Petrov
professor.text: Many people buy bottled water, even though tap water is safe in many cities. Should cities try to reduce the sale of bottled water? Why or why not?

students.name: Zoe
students.text: Yes, because plastic bottles create a lot of waste. Cities could install more free water fountains.

students.name: Mateo
students.text: People should be free to choose. Some people don't like the taste of tap water, and bottled water is convenient.

professor.name: Professor Diaz
professor.text: Some people think that famous athletes and entertainers earn too much money. Do you agree? Why or why not?

students.name: Anna
students.text: Yes. Nurses and teachers do more important work but earn much less. The difference is not fair.

students.name: Luke
students.text: Their careers are short and they bring in a lot of money for their teams and companies, so their salaries make sense.

professor.name: Dr. Schmidt
professor.text: In some countries, students take a year off between high school and university to work or travel. Do you think a gap year is a good idea? Why?

students.name: Ella
students.text: A gap year gives students time to think about what they really want to study. They become more mature.

students.name: Oscar
students.text: Students may lose their study habits during a gap year, and some never go back to school.

professor.name: Professor Yilmaz
professor.text: Many museums now offer virtual tours online. Do you think virtual tours can replace visiting a museum in person? Why or why not?

students.name: Ruby
students.text: Virtual tours are great for people who live far away or can't afford to travel. Everyone can see famous art.

students.name: Adam
students.text: Seeing a painting on a screen is not the same. The size, the colors and the atmosphere are different in person.

professor.name: Dr. Andersen
professor.text: Some people believe that all students should learn to cook at school. Is this a useful subject to teach in schools? Explain your opinion.

students.name: Mia
students.text: Yes, cooking is a basic life skill. If young people can cook, they eat healthier and spend less money.

students.name: Liam
students.text: Parents can teach cooking at home. Schools should focus on academic subjects that parents cannot teach.

professor.name: Professor Clarke
professor.text: Some companies allow employees to choose their own working hours. Do you think flexible working hours are a good idea? Why or why not?

students.name: Laura
students.text: Flexible hours make workers happier because they can organize their day around their families.

students.name: Henry
students.text: If everyone works at different times, it is hard to have meetings and work as a team.

professor.name: Dr. Moreau
professor.text: Some people think that it is better to live in a big city, while others prefer small towns. Where do you think it is better to live, and why?

students.name: Eva
students.text: Big cities offer more jobs, better universities and many cultural activities.

students.name: Daniel
students.text: Small towns are quieter and safer. People know each other, and life is less stressful.

professor.name: Professor Hughes
professor.text: Some teachers let students use calculators in math class, while others do not. Should students be allowed to use calculators? Why or why not?

students.name: Sara
students.text: Calculators save time, so students can focus on understanding the problem instead of simple calculations.

students.name: Max
students.text: If students always use calculators, they will never learn to calculate in their heads.

professor.name: Dr. Ali
professor.text: Many people believe that everyone should do some volunteer work in their community. Should volunteering be required for high school students? Why?

students.name: Julia
students.text: Yes, volunteering teaches young people to care about others and helps the community.

students.name: Ahmed
students.text: Volunteering should be a free choice. If it is required, students will not do it with real interest.

professor.name: Professor Reyes
professor.text: Electric scooters are becoming popular in many cities. Do you think cities should encourage people to use them? Why or why not?

students.name: Nina
students.text: Scooters are cheap and don't produce pollution. They are perfect for short trips.

students.name: George
students.text: They can be dangerous for pedestrians, especially when people ride them on sidewalks.

professor.name: Dr. Ncube
professor.text: Some people think that reading printed books is better than reading on a screen. Which do you prefer for studying, and why?

students.name: Clara
students.text: I remember more when I read printed books. I can write notes in the margins and I don't get distracted.

students.name: Ivan
students.text: E-books are lighter and cheaper. I can carry many books on one device and search for words easily.

professor.name: Professor Evans
professor.text: Some universities give students grades, while others only use 'pass' or 'fail'. Which system do you think is better for learning? Explain.

students.name: Emily
students.text: Grades motivate students to work harder and show employers who performed best.

students.name: Ali
students.text: Pass or fail reduces stress. Students can focus on learning instead of competing for high marks.

professor.name: Dr. Larsen
professor.text: Fast food is popular all over the world. Should governments do more to limit fast food advertising, especially to children? Why or why not?

students.name: Sophie
students.text: Yes, children are easily influenced by ads, and too much fast food causes health problems.

students.name: Tyler
students.text: Parents, not governments, should decide what their children eat. Limiting ads goes too far.

professor.name: Professor Wu
professor.text: Many young people spend a lot of time playing video games. Do you think video games have more positive or negative effects? Explain your opinion.

students.name: Kai
students.text: Some games improve problem-solving and teamwork. They can also be a good way to relax.

students.name: Amelia
students.text: Many young people play too much and don't get enough exercise or sleep.

professor.name: Dr. Popescu
professor.text: Some people believe that tourists should pay an extra tax when they visit popular cities. Is this a fair idea? Why or why not?

students.name: Marta
students.text: Tourists use local services, so a small tax can help pay for cleaning and maintenance.

students.name: Jonas
students.text: An extra tax could make some people stop visiting, and local businesses would lose money.

professor.name: Professor Grant
professor.text: Some students choose their major based on their interests, while others choose based on future salary. Which should be more important when choosing a major?

students.name: Hailey
students.text: Interests are more important. If you enjoy your subject, you will work harder and be more successful.

students.name: Victor
students.text: University is expensive. Students should think about getting a good job after they graduate.

professor.name: Dr. Oyelaran
professor.text: Some cities are planting many trees in streets and parks. Is planting trees the best way for a city to improve the environment? Explain your view.

students.name: Rosa
students.text: Trees clean the air, give shade and make cities cooler in summer. It is a simple and effective solution.

students.name: Felix
students.text: Trees help, but cities also need better public transportation and cleaner energy to really make a difference.

professor.name: Professor Martin
professor.text: Many schools have removed art and music classes to spend more time on math and science. Do you think this is a good decision? Why or why not?

students.name: Lena
students.text: Art and music develop creativity, which is important in every job. Removing them is a mistake.

students.name: Chris
students.text: Math and science skills are needed for many modern jobs, so schools should focus on them.

professor.name: Dr. Sato
professor.text: Some people think that shopping online is better than shopping in stores. Which do you prefer, and why?

students.name: Alina
students.text: Online shopping is faster and I can compare prices easily without leaving home.

students.name: Pedro
students.text: In a store, I can see and touch the product before buying it, so I make fewer mistakes.

professor.name: Professor Kowalski
professor.text: Some people say that students learn more from their mistakes than from their successes. Do you agree? Explain your view with an example.

students.name: Irene
students.text: I agree. When I fail a test, I study the problems carefully and I never make the same mistake again.

students.name: Samir
students.text: Success is also important. When I do well, I feel motivated to continue working hard.

professor.name: Dr. Bianchi
professor.text: Many families now eat meals in front of the television or while using their phones. Is it important for families to eat together without screens? Why?

students.name: Anya
students.text: Yes, meals are the only time many families can talk. Screens stop people from communicating.

students.name: Luis
students.text: Families are busy today. Watching a show together can also be a way to spend time together.

professor.name: Professor Wright
professor.text: Some universities now use artificial intelligence to answer students' questions. Do you think this is helpful for students? Why or why not?

students.name: Freya
students.text: It is helpful because students can get answers at any time, even late at night.

students.name: Hugo
students.text: Computers sometimes give wrong answers. Students need real people who understand their situation.

professor.name: Dr. Jensen
professor.text: Some people think that children should have their own smartphones by the age of ten. Others think they should wait until they are older. What do you think?

students.name: Maya
students.text: A phone helps children stay in contact with their parents and feel safe.

students.name: Owen
students.text: Ten is too young. Children may spend too much time online and see things that are not appropriate.

professor.name: Professor Ahmed
professor.text: Many people believe that exams are the best way to test students' knowledge. Others prefer projects or presentations. Which method do you think is better?

students.name: Kate
students.text: Exams are fair because every student answers the same questions in the same time.

students.name: Diego
students.text: Projects show what students can really do. They also teach skills like research and teamwork.

professor.name: Dr. Richter
professor.text: Some people think that it is important to keep traditional festivals and customs. Others think they are less important in the modern world. What is your opinion?

students.name: Ines
students.text: Traditions connect us to our history and our families. We should protect them.

students.name: Tobias
students.text: Some traditions are old-fashioned. It is natural for cultures to change over time.

professor.name: Professor Nakamura
professor.text: Many cities have problems with food waste. Should restaurants and supermarkets be required to donate food they cannot sell? Explain your view.

students.name: Camila
students.text: Yes, it is terrible to throw away good food when many people are hungry.

students.name: Erik
students.text: Businesses might worry about safety rules. The government should help them, not force them.

professor.name: Dr. Walsh
professor.text: Some people think teenagers should be able to vote at sixteen. Do you agree or disagree? Why?

students.name: Harper
students.text: Sixteen-year-olds pay taxes if they work, so they should have a voice in decisions.

students.name: Nathan
students.text: Most sixteen-year-olds don't know enough about politics yet. Eighteen is a better age.

professor.name: Professor Da Silva
professor.text: Many students feel stressed during exam periods. What is the most effective thing universities can do to help students manage stress?

students.name: Bianca
students.text: Universities should offer free counseling and workshops about stress.

students.name: Jake
students.text: Spreading exams over the whole semester would help more than any workshop.

professor.name: Dr. Levi
professor.text: Some people prefer to have many friends, while others prefer a few close friends. Which do you think is better, and why?

students.name: Sienna
students.text: A few close friends are better. You can trust them completely and share your problems.

students.name: Matthew
students.text: Having many friends gives you more opportunities and different perspectives.

professor.name: Professor Osei
professor.text: Some people believe that governments should spend more money on public parks. Others think the money should go to hospitals or schools. What is your view?

students.name: Elena
students.text: Parks are important for health because people can exercise and relax there.

students.name: Robert
students.text: Hospitals and schools are more urgent. Parks are nice, but they are not a basic need.

professor.name: Dr. Berg
professor.text: Many people now listen to podcasts to learn new things. Do you think podcasts are a good way to learn? Why or why not?

students.name: Tara
students.text: Podcasts are great because you can learn while you walk, cook or travel.

students.name: Simon
students.text: It is hard to concentrate on a podcast while doing other things, so you don't remember much.

professor.name: Professor Hall
professor.text: Some people think that learning to play a musical instrument should be required in school. Do you agree? Explain your opinion.

students.name: Lucy
students.text: Playing music improves concentration and memory, which helps with other subjects too.

students.name: Aaron
students.text: Not everyone is interested in music. Students should be able to choose their activities.

professor.name: Dr. Quintero
professor.text: Many young adults continue living with their parents after they finish university. Do you think this is a good or bad choice? Why?

students.name: Valeria
students.text: It is a smart choice because they can save money before renting their own home.

students.name: Connor
students.text: Living alone teaches independence. Young adults should leave home as soon as they can.

professor.name: Dr. Morales
professor.text: Many universities now ask students to do volunteer work before they graduate. Should volunteering be required for a degree, or should it stay a personal choice? Why?

students.name: Ethan
students.text: It should be required. Volunteering teaches skills you don't learn in class, like working with people from different backgrounds.

students.name: Priya
students.text: I think it should be a choice. Many students already work to pay for their studies, so they don't have extra time.
